basis: Inherited progressive cardiac conduction disease; dizziness, syncope and dyspnea do not establish damage to other organs.
AAGAB-related punctate hyperkeratosis of palms and soles; no established extracutaneous damage.
Acute lacrimal canalicular inflammation is typically a localized bacterial infection.
Malignant tumor originating in visceral pleura; pleura belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Ventricular tachyarrhythmia; underlying causes do not establish additional organs for this rhythm disorder.
Congenital channel connecting ascending aorta and ventricle; associated valve, coronary and ventricular abnormalities remain cardiovascular.
Mitochondrial dysfunction is metabolic; encephalopathy/neuropathy and skeletal myopathy each commonly affect >30%; other organs vary substantially across subtypes.
Malignant precursor lymphocytes define a hematologic neoplasm; the umbrella includes lymphoblastic lymphoma, requiring the immune mechanism axis.
Deficient intestinal brush-border carbohydrate digestion defines both intestinal malabsorption and a disorder of sugar metabolism.
Inherited antibody immunodeficiency; neutropenia reported in 1/1 patient supports hematologic involvement with limited evidence; recurrent infections alone add no organ.
Sensory/autonomic neuropathy with defining anhidrosis and sweat-gland aplasia; fractures, joint injury, tooth loss and osteomyelitis are secondary complications.
Schwann-cell nerve sheath tumor, usually arising from spinal nerve roots; pigmentation does not imply skin origin.
Defining abnormalities involve cornea, lens, intraocular fetal vasculature and retinal/iris coloboma; no extraocular organ established.
Inherited retinal degeneration with visual loss; retinal vascular attenuation is part of ocular disease, not systemic vascular disease.
Carcinoma originates in salivary ducts; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis. Metastatic destinations are not defining organs.
Intellectual disability is the shared defining feature; blepharophimosis and marfanoid habitus vary across subtypes without established common functional damage.
Benign neoplasm occupying the trachea, which belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Pathologic lymphoid proliferation defines hematologic disease in an immunodeficiency-associated setting; no other organ is consistently specified.
Ovarian epithelial malignancy is reproductive, not an endocrine-gland tumor; associated hypercalcemia does not establish common direct endocrine damage.
SCN2A-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with seizures, developmental impairment and brain atrophy.
Cataract 14/15, deafness and ID 15/15 define syndrome; pericarditis 6/15 (40%); skeletal (12/15) and dental (6/15) anomalies omitted under the four-axis cap.
Ependymal tumor originating in the spinal cord.
Sialic acid metabolism/storage disorder; neurodevelopmental impairment occurs commonly (>30%) across typical forms; organ enlargement alone does not establish damage.
Substance dependence is outside the axes; overdose, injection-related infections and other separately diagnosed complications are not intrinsic organ labels.
Granulomatous lesion of orbital tissues; unspecified etiology does not establish an infectious or autoimmune disease.
